source.title: Scaling MLPs: A Tale of Inductive Bias
source.authors: Gregor Bachmann; Sotiris Anagnostidis; Thomas Hofmann

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports MLP results under batch-size, optimizer, dropout, and architecture changes, using its own downstream accuracy measures rather than the claim versions’ original methods.
record.gate_note: The study cites prior random-label memorization work and several optimizer, batch-size, and convolution studies; those cited results are not rows. Figure 4 does not provide recoverable batch-size values in the supplied text. Figure 8's ablation values are also not recoverable; only the authors' textual summary is recorded.
record.test_reason: The study tests convolutional versus fully connected image classification, batch-size effects at fixed epoch counts, and dropout in scaled MLP training and transfer settings. AdamW versus LION does not test V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that scale can compensate for MLPs' weak vision inductive bias and that MLPs largely mirror modern architectures, while augmentation and batch-size effects differ substantially. Larger batches improve downstream performance, and compute-optimal MLP scaling favors additional training examples.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines scaled MLPs in modern vision pre-training and downstream evaluation, using LION, augmentation, and related ablations rather than the original claim versions' specific recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset augmentation strongly changes MLP performance; larger batch sizes improve reported downstream accuracy across training times; replacing LION with AdamW decreases downstream performance; dropout has a small positive effect. Test-time augmentation also improves reported transfer results.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing LION with AdamW reduces downstream linear-probing performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects MLP transfer performance, with LION outperforming AdamW in this ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: MLP downstream error follows scaling laws as parameter count, dataset size, and compute increase, without establishing interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaled MLP pre-training improves transfer performance predictably, with compute-optimal allocation favoring more examples.

record.problems: The architecture comparison uses different image resolutions and unmatched training recipes. Batch-size and ablation values in figures are not recoverable from the supplied text. The dropout effect is only described as small, without a numerical estimate.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to tested versions were omitted. Cited prior studies and their results are excluded.

untested.parts: No paired natural-label and random-label fitting or held-out accuracy experiment.
Scaling experiments do not establish zero training error or identify widths beyond the interpolation threshold.

No isolation of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, or convolution-initialized fully connected networks. Architecture comparisons do not match augmentation, resolution, and training recipes.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD or momentum-SGD comparison under comparable tuning; no test of switching optimizers or broader tuning.
No language-model experiment, controlled recipe-adaptation comparison, or identified workload-dependent critical batch size. The recorded endpoint is downstream linear-probing accuracy.
No very-small-training-set exception, excessive-dropout underfitting threshold, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining.

missing.what: Additional scratch-trained architecture comparisons: S-MLP with augmentation reaches 72.3/44.5/27.3/26.8% after 5000 epochs; B-MLP with augmentation reaches 75.4/50.4/31.2/31.7%, versus ResNet18's 93.2/75.6/68.9/69.7% on CIFAR10/CIFAR100/TinyImageNet/ImageNet. These show that the convolutional advantage persists beyond the unaugmented S-MLP comparison recorded in R2–R5.

record.verdict_notes: Unmatched architecture recipes qualify causal interpretation, but are not themselves evidence against V3. V5 already includes conditions without a large-batch penalty, so the MLP result limits its scope rather than challenging the entire version. No external sources were consulted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural labels are not tested.
No width sweep tied to zero training error or test error beyond an interpolation threshold is reported.

The architecture comparison is not a controlled comparison of matched convolutional and fully connected networks trained with the same recipe; no sparse-local-connection or convolution-initialized MLP comparison.
Compares AdamW with LION, not the adaptive-optimizer versus SGD or momentum-SGD comparisons in the version; no broader hyperparameter-tuning study or language benchmark.
No language models, fixed-epoch large-batch penalty, or adaptations such as warmup and normalization changes are tested.
Reports only a small positive dropout effect in the supplied text; does not establish the very-small-training-set exception or an underfitting threshold.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal or retraining experiment.
